messages:
steph: Quick report: users hitting missing trace headers when using AsyncClient in python. Our httpx async path doesn't propagate OpenTelemetry context by default.

ryan: Do we have a small repro? async or sync?

steph: async. Minimal: 
```py
from redwood import AsyncClient
from opentelemetry import trace
client = AsyncClient(api_key=...)
tracer = trace.get_tracer(__name__)
async with tracer.start_as_current_span('foo'):
    await client.chat.complete('hi')
```
No traceparent header recorded on egress.

nina: I dug into transport; headers are composed in a helper that reads env and request args but never calls propagators.inject. Sync path that uses requests picks up requests-instrumentation but async path is doing its own header assembly.

zara: Two proposed fixes: (1) Optional integration that calls propagators.inject when opentelemetry is available, (2) a middleware hook for customers to inject custom headers (x-redwood-request-id, tenant, etc).

ryan: Agree. Middleware should be simple: signature like (req: MutableMapping[str,str], call_next) -> Response or Awaitable[Response]. Need to support both sync and async middlewares.

steph: Typing follow-up: streaming endpoints currently return Any in stubs which breaks mypy for consumers. We should change to AsyncIterator[Union[str, TokenChunk]] and provide generics.

nina: Implementation details: lazy import opentelemetry and only call propagators.inject(headers) if present. Add an extra optional dependency redwood[tracing].
Also preserve any user-provided "x-redwood-request-id" and only generate a UUID if absent.

zara: Tests: add an httpx mock transport capturing outgoing headers and use InMemorySpanExporter to assert traceparent exists after propagation. Add sync+async tests.

ryan: UX: config options on Client: propagate_tracing: bool (default False for now), add_middleware(fn) and a built-in middleware: RequestIdMiddleware with preserve_existing=True. Document FIFO middleware order.

steph: Docs: add an example in examples/fastapi_otel.py showing FastAPI dependency that attaches request-id to client via middleware and shows OTLP exporter config for local dev.

nina: CI note: mypy failure in other repos due to streaming typing changes. We'll need to coordinate a dep bump and release notes.

zara: Small nit: header casing should be normalized to lower-case keys internally to avoid duplicates. Also log the generated request-id at INFO with key redwood.request_id for correlation.

ops-bot: CI started for branch fix/async-otel (PR #498) \u2014 running tests: linux-py3.11, mypy, flake8.

ryan: For backwards compatibility, add Client(..., propagate_tracing=False) default. We'll flip in next minor after migration window and announce in changelog.

steph: Workaround for users today: call propagators.inject(headers) and pass extra_headers. Example: 
```py
from opentelemetry.propagators.textmap import inject
h = {}
inject(h)
await client.chat.complete('hi', extra_headers=h)
```
Not ideal but documented in migration note.

nina: I'll draft the RFC for middleware shape and typing Protocols (MiddlewareSync/MiddlewareAsync) plus Request/Response TypedDicts.

zara: I'll add the sample FastAPI snippet and the unit test harness capturing headers.

ops-bot: PR #498 tests failed on mypy (streaming typing). Filing ticket: DE-787.

steph: Thanks team. ping me if you want to pair on the async test tomorrow morning.
